gloss: nanban-zuke; fried fish, chicken, or vegetables marinated in sweet vinegar with chili and onion

definitions.gloss: nanban-zuke; fried fish, chicken, or vegetables marinated in sweet vinegar sauce
definitions.explanation: A Japanese dish in which fried fish, chicken, or vegetables are marinated in a sweet-sour sauce of vinegar, soy, sugar, sliced onion, and chili pepper. Served chilled or at room temperature; the flavors deepen as it sits.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今晩|こんばん}→今晩：02882_konban⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦おかず→おかず：08272_okazu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{鯵|あじ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{南蛮漬|なんばんづ}けだ。
examples.english: Tonight's side dish is horse mackerel nanban-zuke.

examples.japanese: {南蛮漬|なんばんづ}け⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{冷|ひ}やして→冷やす：02403_hiyasu⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{美味|おい}しい→美味しい：00740_oishii⟧。

⟦{揚|あ}げた→揚げる：16879_ageru⟧⟦{鶏肉|とりにく}→鶏肉：02919_toriniku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{玉|たま}ねぎ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{唐辛子|とうがらし}→唐辛子：11871_tougarashi⟧{入|い}り⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{南蛮酢|なんばんず}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{漬|つ}けて→漬ける：09861_tsukeru⟧、{南蛮漬|なんばんづ}け⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: I deep-fried chicken and marinated it in nanban vinegar with onion and chili to make nanban-zuke.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{南蛮|なんばん}→南蛮：12304_nanban⟧ (literally "southern barbarian," a historical term for Portuguese and Spanish traders) plus {漬|つ}け (pickled, marinated). The dish is thought to derive from the southern-European technique of preserving fried fish in vinegar.

USAGE:
- Most often made with small whole fish (especially {鯵|あじ}) or chicken pieces
- Marinade combines vinegar, soy, sugar, sliced onion, and dried chili
- Best after several hours so the flavors penetrate; commonly eaten as a make-ahead dish

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鯵|あじ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{南蛮漬|なんばんづ}け: horse mackerel nanban-zuke
- {鶏|とり}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{南蛮漬|なんばんづ}け: chicken nanban-zuke
- {南蛮漬|なんばんづ}け⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to make into nanban-zuke

RELATED WORDS:
- {チキン南蛮|ちきんなんばん}: a Miyazaki specialty of fried chicken with tartar sauce — uses similar nanban vinegar but is served warm
